Alex, Ben, Chris, and David participated in a chess tournament every month. At the end of the year, Alex had won seven more games than Ben, but Chris had won 4 games fewer than Ben. David had won 2 games more than Chris did. If David won a total of 18 games, how many more games did Alex win than did David? Since David won 18 games and he won 2 games more than Chris, Chris won $18 - 2 = 16$ games. Chris won 4 games fewer than Ben, so Ben won $16 + 4 = 20$ games. Alex won 7 more games than Ben, so Alex won $20 + 7 = 27$ games. Now we know that Alex won 27 games and David won 18 games. The difference between Alex's and David's wins is $27 - 18 = 9$. So Alex won \boxed{9} more games than David did.

Online Learning of Rested and Restless Bandits In this paper we study the online learning problem involving rested and restless multiarmed bandits with multiple plays. The system consists of a single player/user and a set of K finite-state discrete-time Markov chains (arms) with unknown state spaces and statistics. At each time step the player can play M arms. In the realm of physics, entropy represents the degree of disorder in a system. Because systems tend to degrade over time, thermodynamic energy becomes less available to do mechanical work. In cryptography, entropy has a distinct but similar meaning. In cryptography, entropy refers to the randomness collected by a system for use in algorithms that require random data. A lack of good entropy can leave a cryptosystem vulnerable and unable to encrypt data securely.
